body:
A closed surface encloses a +4.0 μC charge at its center. A +4.0 μC charge sits outside the surface. The inside charge is moved to a spot near the surface (still inside), and the outside charge is moved closer to the surface (still outside). What happens to the net electric flux through the surface?

Choices:
A. It stays the same only if the inside charge returns to the center
B. It increases, because the field at the surface is stronger
C. It stays the same
D. It decreases, because part of the surface is now closer to the charge

The potential along the x-axis consists of straight-line segments: V = 10 V at x = 0, V = 2 V at x = 0.20 m, and V = 11 V at x = 0.50 m. Which choice gives E_x in each segment?

Choices:
A. +10 V/m for 0 < x < 0.20 m, then +22 V/m for 0.20 m < x < 0.50 m
B. +40 V/m for 0 < x < 0.20 m, then −30 V/m for 0.20 m < x < 0.50 m
C. −2 V/m throughout
D. +30 V/m for 0 < x < 0.20 m, then −40 V/m for 0.20 m < x < 0.50 m

A smooth potential V(x) has a local maximum at x = 1.0 m and a local minimum at x = 3.0 m, with no other stationary points between them. Which statement about E_x is correct?

Choices:
A. E_x is zero at both points and negative between them
B. E_x is most positive at x = 1.0 m and most negative at x = 3.0 m
C. E_x is nonzero at both points because V is not zero there
D. E_x is zero at both points and positive between them

Capacitor 1 has circular plates of radius R separated by d. Capacitor 2 has circular plates of radius 2R separated by 3d. Both are vacuum-filled. What is C₂/C₁, neglecting edge effects?

Choices:
A. 4/3
B. 2/3
C. 12
D. 1/12

A positive point charge sits just outside one face of an imaginary closed cube, not touching it. What is the total electric flux through the entire surface of the cube due to this outside charge?

Choices:
A. Negative, because the field is strongest at the nearest face
B. q/ε₀, because the charge’s field passes through the surface
C. Zero, because each field line entering the cube also leaves it
D. Positive, because the field at the near face points into the cube

A charge +Q lies inside a closed surface. A charge −Q is then placed just outside the surface. Compared with the situation before the second charge was added, which statement is correct?

Choices:
A. The net flux becomes zero because the total charge is zero
B. The net flux and the field at every surface point are both unchanged
C. The net flux is unchanged, but the field at points on the surface changes
D. The net flux becomes negative because the new charge is negative

A charged solid metal object sits in electrostatic equilibrium. Why must the electric field just outside its surface be perpendicular to the surface?

Choices:
A. Electric field lines always cross every surface at right angles
B. Excess charge spreads uniformly over any conductor, and uniform charge gives only a perpendicular field
C. A steady surface current cancels any part of the field along the surface
D. A component along the surface would push charges along it, so equilibrium allows none

A parallel-plate capacitor is charged by a battery, which is then disconnected. A dielectric with κ = 4 is slipped in to fill the space between the plates completely. The energy stored in the capacitor becomes

Choices:
A. one-sixteenth of its original value
B. unchanged
C. one-fourth of its original value
D. four times its original value

The electric potential along the x-axis is constant at 10 V for x < 2.0 m, decreases linearly to 4.0 V between x = 2.0 m and x = 5.0 m, and is constant at 4.0 V for x > 5.0 m. What is the electric field in the region 2.0 m < x < 5.0 m?

Choices:
A. Zero, because V is nonzero there
B. 6.0 V/m in the +x direction
C. 0.50 V/m in the +x direction
D. 2.0 V/m in the +x direction

A solid insulating sphere of radius R carries charge distributed uniformly throughout its volume. The electric field magnitude at the surface of the sphere is E_s. What is the field magnitude at a distance R/3 from the center?

Choices:
A. 3E_s
B. E_s/3
C. E_s/9
D. 9E_s
